sets.relationshipLabel: A category of material or plant part, and a specific kind within it
sets.explanation: Wood and root are general terms; hardwood and taproot name a specific kind within each category.

sets.relationshipLabel: A craftsman and the product their craft is about
sets.explanation: A carpenter's craft yields furniture, just as a papermaker's craft yields paper.

sets.relationshipLabel: A plant part and a feature it inherently has
sets.explanation: A trunk inherently has rings, just as a leaf inherently has veins — an internal feature, not a subtype.

sets.relationshipLabel: The opening and closing moments of a tree's or season's life-span
sets.explanation: Planting begins a tree's life as felling ends it, just as budding begins a season's growth as withering ends it.

glossary.definition: the act of cutting something down so it falls to the ground

definitions.definition: the solid material that trees are made of, used for building and burning.
a dense, sturdy kind of wood that comes from slow-growing trees like oak.
the part of a plant that grows underground and pulls in water and nutrients.
a thick, single main root that digs straight down deep into the soil.
someone skilled at building and shaping things out of wood.
things like tables and chairs that you use to sit, eat, or store stuff.
someone whose job is turning pulp into sheets of paper.
the thin material you write, print, or draw on.
the thick woody stem of a tree that holds it upright.
circular lines inside a tree trunk that show its age, one per year.
the flat green part of a plant that catches sunlight to make food.
a thin line running through a leaf that carries water and nutrients.
putting a seed or seedling into the ground so it can start growing.
the act of cutting something down so it falls to the ground.
the moment new growth starts pushing out on a plant, like tiny buds appearing.
drying up and shrinking as a plant loses its life and freshness.
